stated: The Conservative Party will ensure councils have the powers needed to manage the uncontrolled growth of holiday lets, which can cause nuisance to local residents and 'hollowing out' of communities.

source.quote: We will ensure councils have the powers they need to manage the uncontrolled growth of holiday lets, which can cause nuisance to local residents and a hollowing out of communities.

bearing_set.reason: Holiday lets convert residential stock into short-term accommodation, reducing housing supply and driving up rents/prices for local residents; giving councils regulatory powers directly addresses housing availability and affordability in affected communities.

The policy explicitly targets community 'hollowing out' — managing holiday let growth would preserve more year-round residents, directly affecting social trust, civic participation and sense of belonging in affected communities.

New council regulatory powers to limit what property owners can do with their own homes is a concrete new state coercive constraint on property rights — a liberty cost that falls squarely within O10's scope regardless of the housing benefit it produces.

membership_note: Three genuine bearings: the housing-supply benefit (O1), the explicit community-cohesion rationale (O15), and the liberty cost of new coercive powers over private property use (O10). Tourism/local-economy effects on O13 are real in principle but the policy only proposes 'managing' growth (not abolishing the sector), making the aggregate prosperity impact too diffuse and speculative to clear the non-negligible bar.
